fact: The Malian government inaugurated its National Data Centre in Bamako around the weekend before 2 Feb 2026 (date is the article's publication date, no event date given); the ministry says it gives administrations, companies, start-ups and technical partners a hosting environment and will host mutualised AES infrastructure short term.

fact: The Malian government describes the National Data Centre in Bamako as a Tier III facility (operator's own statement, no certification named); event date is the article's publication date.

fact: Mali's Ministry of Communication, Digital Economy and Administration Modernisation inaugurated the Tier III National Data Centre, which the government says will provide secure hosting for the Malian state's strategic data, e-administration platforms and public digital services (stated in the future tense; inauguration reported 'over the weekend' before the 2026-02-02 article).

fact: ITU's 2022 report says the Malian state telecom infrastructure company SMTD runs a government data centre offering colocation, integrated data centre, IaaS, SaaS and backup services to clients; the document does not say whether clients beyond government are served, and gives 2022 as its date.

ITU states the SMTD data centre, which offers colocation, IaaS, SaaS and backup services, is run by the Société malienne de transmission et de diffusion, described as the company that manages the State's telecommunications infrastructure, and that the Government of Mali set up the two data centres through its agencies.

ITU states the AGETIC, a government agency under the ministry MCENMA, runs a data centre providing hosting (IaaS, SaaS, backup) to the public administration, with a real-time-replicated DR site; the document gives the year only.
